issues.description: The UML/problem statement specifies RollerCoaster.numberOfLoopings as an int and requires constructors to accept attributes with the same types and order. In the solution, RollerCoaster's constructor declares the parameter numberOfLoopings as double (and casts it to int inside), which conflicts with the UML/spec and the stated constructor requirement. This mismatch can confuse students about the correct constructor signature they must implement and violates the explicit constructor-parameter-type rule in the task.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the RollerCoaster constructor parameter type in the solution to int to match the UML/spec: public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings) { super(name, abbreviation); this.numberOfLoopings = numberOfLoopings; }. Update any callers accordingly (e.g., LaunchedRollerCoaster can continue to pass an int). This aligns the implementation with the UML and the exercise requirement that constructor parameters match attribute types.
